UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Stores user-specific settings and preferences, linked to an external authentication system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity, typically provided by an external authentication system.

prayerCalculationMethod.description: The preferred method for calculating daily prayer times (e.g., 'MuslimWorldLeague', 'ISNA').

madhab.description: The user's preferred Madhab (school of thought) for prayer time adjustments (e.g., 'Hanafi', 'Shafii').

latitude.description: The geographical latitude of the user's location, used for prayer time calculations.

longitude.description: The geographical longitude of the user's location, used for prayer time calculations.

timezone.description: The user's local timezone (e.g., 'America/New_York'), crucial for displaying correct prayer times.

Author.title: Author
Author.description: Represents an author of scholarly works, Tafsir, or Hadith commentaries.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Author entity.

name.description: The full name of the author.

biography.description: A brief biographical summary of the author.

era.description: The historical era during which the author lived or was prominent (e.g., 'Classical', 'Contemporary').

Topic.title: Topic
Topic.description: Categorizes various Islamic subjects, used for organizing texts, quizzes, and other content.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Topic entity.

name.description: The name of the topic (e.g., 'Aqidah', 'Fiqh', 'Hadith Sciences').

description.description: A brief description of the topic.

textIds.description: References to Text entities associated with this topic. (Relationship: Topic N:N Text)

quizIds.description: References to Quiz entities associated with this topic. (Relationship: Topic N:N Quiz)

Text.title: Text
Text.description: Represents a classical Islamic text or scholarly work in the library.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Text entity.

title.description: The title of the scholarly text.

authorId.description: Reference to the Author of the text. (Relationship: Author 1:N Text)

language.description: The primary language of the text (e.g., 'ar' for Arabic, 'en' for English).

publicationYear.description: The year the text was originally published or compiled.

contentUri.description: A URI pointing to the full content of the text, stored externally.

description.description: A brief summary or introduction to the text.

methodology.description: The theological or jurisprudential methodology associated with the text (e.g., 'Salafi/Athari').

topicIds.description: References to Topic entities that categorize this text. (Relationship: Text N:N Topic)

Adhkar.title: Adhkar
Adhkar.description: Represents a daily supplication (dhikr) with Arabic text, transliteration, and translation.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Adhkar entity.

transliteration.description: Phonetic transliteration of the Arabic text.

translationEnglish.description: The English translation of the supplication.

sourceReference.description: The authentic source of the supplication (e.g., 'Sahih Muslim 123', 'Fortress of the Muslim').

category.description: The category or time for the supplication (e.g., 'Morning', 'Evening', 'Before Sleep', 'After Prayer').

Surah.title: Surah
Surah.description: Represents a chapter (Surah) of the Holy Quran.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Surah entity.

number.description: The ordinal number of the Surah in the Quran (1-114).

nameArabic.description: The name of the Surah in Arabic.

nameEnglish.description: The English translation of the Surah's name.

revelationPlace.description: Indicates whether the Surah was revealed in Mecca or Medina ('Meccan' or 'Medinan').

ayahCount.description: The total number of verses (Ayat) in the Surah.

Ayah.title: Ayah
Ayah.description: Represents a single verse (Ayah) of the Holy Quran.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Ayah entity.

surahId.description: Reference to the Surah to which this Ayah belongs. (Relationship: Surah 1:N Ayah)

ayahNumber.description: The verse number within its Surah.

arabicText.description: The Arabic text of the Ayah.

translationEnglish.description: The English translation of the Ayah.

TafsirBook.title: TafsirBook
TafsirBook.description: Represents a complete book of Quranic exegesis (Tafsir).

id.description: Unique identifier for the TafsirBook entity.

title.description: The title of the Tafsir book.

authorId.description: Reference to the Author of the Tafsir book. (Relationship: Author 1:N TafsirBook)

language.description: The primary language of the Tafsir book.

description.description: A brief description of the Tafsir book.

TafsirEntry.title: TafsirEntry
TafsirEntry.description: Represents a specific commentary passage from a Tafsir book for an Ayah.

id.description: Unique identifier for the TafsirEntry entity.

tafsirBookId.description: Reference to the TafsirBook from which this entry originates. (Relationship: TafsirBook 1:N TafsirEntry)

ayahId.description: Reference to the Ayah that this tafsir entry explains. (Relationship: Ayah 1:N TafsirEntry)

commentaryText.description: The actual text of the commentary for the Ayah.

language.description: The language of this specific commentary entry, which might differ from the book's primary language if translated.

HadithCollection.title: HadithCollection
HadithCollection.description: Represents a compilation of Hadith, such as Sahih Bukhari or Sahih Muslim.

id.description: Unique identifier for the HadithCollection entity.

name.description: The name of the Hadith collection (e.g., 'Sahih Bukhari').

compiler.description: The name of the scholar who compiled this Hadith collection.

description.description: A brief description of the Hadith collection.

language.description: The original language of the Hadith collection (e.g., 'ar').

id.description: Unique identifier for the Hadith entity.

hadithCollectionId.description: Reference to the HadithCollection this Hadith belongs to. (Relationship: HadithCollection 1:N Hadith)

hadithNumber.description: The specific number or reference for the Hadith within its collection.

arabicText.description: The Arabic text of the Hadith.

translationEnglish.description: The English translation of the Hadith.

grade.description: The authenticity grade of the Hadith (e.g., 'Sahih', 'Hasan', 'Da'if').

HadithCommentaryBook.title: HadithCommentaryBook
HadithCommentaryBook.description: Represents a complete book of Hadith commentary.

id.description: Unique identifier for the HadithCommentaryBook entity.

title.description: The title of the Hadith commentary book.

authorId.description: Reference to the Author of the commentary book. (Relationship: Author 1:N HadithCommentaryBook)

language.description: The primary language of the Hadith commentary book.

description.description: A brief description of the Hadith commentary book.

HadithCommentaryEntry.title: HadithCommentaryEntry
HadithCommentaryEntry.description: Represents a specific commentary passage from a Hadith commentary book for a Hadith.

id.description: Unique identifier for the HadithCommentaryEntry entity.

hadithCommentaryBookId.description: Reference to the HadithCommentaryBook from which this entry originates. (Relationship: HadithCommentaryBook 1:N HadithCommentaryEntry)

hadithId.description: Reference to the Hadith that this commentary entry explains. (Relationship: Hadith 1:N HadithCommentaryEntry)

commentaryText.description: The actual text of the commentary for the Hadith.

language.description: The language of this specific commentary entry.

SeerahEvent.title: SeerahEvent
SeerahEvent.description: Represents an event from the biography (Seerah) of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).

id.description: Unique identifier for the SeerahEvent entity.

title.description: The title or name of the event.

description.description: A detailed description of the event, its significance, and related narratives.

eventDate.description: The approximate date and time of the event.

locationDescription.description: A description of the geographical location where the event took place.

Quiz.title: Quiz
Quiz.description: Represents an Islamic quiz on various topics.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Quiz entity.

description.description: A brief description or introduction to the quiz.

topicIds.description: References to Topic entities that categorize this quiz. (Relationship: Quiz N:N Topic)

Question.title: Question
Question.description: Represents a single question within an Islamic quiz.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Question entity.

quizId.description: Reference to the Quiz to which this question belongs. (Relationship: Quiz 1:N Question)

text.description: The text of the quiz question.

explanation.description: An explanation for the correct answer, displayed after the user attempts the question.

AnswerOption.title: AnswerOption
AnswerOption.description: Represents an answer option for a multiple-choice quiz question.

id.description: Unique identifier for the AnswerOption entity.

questionId.description: Reference to the Question this answer option belongs to. (Relationship: Question 1:N AnswerOption)

text.description: The text of the answer option.

isCorrect.description: Indicates whether this answer option is the correct one for the question.

UserBookmark.title: UserBookmark
UserBookmark.description: Stores a user's bookmark for a specific piece of content.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserBookmark entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who created the bookmark. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N UserBookmark)

entityType.description: The type of entity being bookmarked (e.g., 'Text', 'Ayah', 'Hadith', 'SeerahEvent', 'Adhkar').

entityId.description: The unique identifier of the specific content entity being bookmarked.

contextLocation.description: A description of the specific location within the entity (e.g., 'Page 123', 'Ayah 3:15', 'Hadith 45', 'Specific paragraph').

createdAt.description: The date and time when the bookmark was created.

UserNote.title: UserNote
UserNote.description: Stores personal notes added by a user to specific content passages.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserNote entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who created the note. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N UserNote)

entityType.description: The type of entity to which the note is attached (e.g., 'Text', 'Ayah', 'Hadith').

entityId.description: The unique identifier of the specific content entity being noted.

startContext.description: Describes the starting point of the content selection associated with the note (e.g., 'Ayah 3:15, word 5', 'Paragraph 2, line 3').

endContext.description: Describes the ending point of the content selection associated with the note (optional, for multi-word or multi-line selections).

noteText.description: The actual text of the user's personal note.

createdAt.description: The date and time when the note was created.

updatedAt.description: The date and time when the note was last updated.

Video.title: Video
Video.description: Represents a scholarly video from a verified YouTube channel.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Video entity.

title.description: The title of the video lecture.

url.description: The YouTube URL of the video.

author.description: The scholar or speaker delivering the lecture.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to be secure, scalable, and debuggable by strictly adhering to the core design principles. The primary strategy involves a clear segregation of publicly accessible, static content from user-specific, private data, and extensive use of path-based authorization and denormalization.

**Authorization Independence (CRITICAL) & QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**

1.  **Public/Static Content Collections:** All core informational entities like 'Author', 'Topic', 'Text', 'Adhkar', 'Surah', 'Ayah', 'TafsirBook', 'TafsirEntry', 'HadithCollection', 'Hadith', 'HadithCommentaryBook', 'HadithCommentaryEntry', 'SeerahEvent', 'Quiz', 'Question', 'AnswerOption', and 'Video' are organized into top-level collections or subcollections with homogeneous security postures (e.g., `/authors`, `/videos`). These collections are intended to be publicly readable by all users, authenticated or not. This design choice inherently ensures **Authorization Independence** because access to these documents does not rely on any parent document's attributes or `get()` calls within security rules. The rules simply allow universal read access. This also directly supports **QAPs** (Queries are not Filters) as any read or list operation on these collections will return all accessible documents, without the need for server-side filtering by security rules, thus optimizing performance and simplifying rule logic. The 'read-only' nature for all documents in these collections satisfies the **Structural Segregation** mandate.

2.  **User-Owned Data Collections:** User-specific data, including 'UserProfile', 'UserBookmark', and 'UserNote', are organized under a dedicated `/users/{userId}` hierarchy (e.g., `/users/{userId}/user_profiles/{userId}`, `/users/{userId}/bookmarks/{bookmarkId}`, `/users/{userId}/notes/{noteId}`).
    *   **Denormalization for Authorization Independence:** For `UserProfile`, the document's ID is set to `request.auth.uid`, and the `id` field within the document is denormalized to `userId`, mirroring the path parameter. Similarly, for `UserBookmark` and `UserNote`, the `userId` field within each document is explicitly denormalized to match the `{userId}` wildcard in their respective paths. This ensures that the ownership information is directly present within each document. Consequently, security rules can evaluate `request.auth.uid == resource.data.userId` or `request.auth.uid == {userId}` without needing to perform `get()` calls to check parent documents for ownership, achieving **Authorization Independence**. This structure also guarantees that **QAPs** are met for user-specific data; a user can only query and list their own bookmarks or notes (`/users/myUid/bookmarks`), and the security rules will only permit access to documents where `resource.data.userId == request.auth.uid`, effectively enforcing ownership at the path level and within the document data itself.

**Debuggability & Clarity of Intent:** The use of descriptive collection names and wildcards (e.g., `{userId}`, `{surahId}`) explicitly communicates the purpose and ownership of the data. The simple `request.auth.uid == resource.data.userId` rule pattern for private data is easy to write, understand, and debug, making authorization intent transparent.

**DBAC (Database-Backed Access Control):** The design relies solely on `request.auth.uid` for user authentication and the `userId` field (denormalized within documents or implied by path) for authorization, requiring no custom claims or complex role management. This keeps the authorization model robust and straightforward.

**Invariants:** The structural path (`/users/{userId}/...`) combined with denormalized `userId` fields in `UserBookmark` and `UserNote` documents creates a strong invariant for ownership, which can be easily enforced by security rules. Timestamps (`createdAt`, `updatedAt`) for user-owned data are also directly present in the documents, allowing for rule-based validation of their integrity.
